case_scope: United Kingdom non-dom reform and FIG transition

jurisdictional_mobility_gate.note: The UK reform is a genuine residence-tax alignment repair, but it remains a watch case because FIG relief, transitional/trust planning, and behavioural response are not yet administratively visible.

non_dom_or_preferential_newcomer_tax_reg.note: The non-dom regime ended for future tax treatment, but four-year FIG relief creates a preferential newcomer rail that must be scored against ordinary long-term residents and trust/offshore planning.

high_wealth_exit_threat.note: Exit-threat claims must remain counterweighted: OBR/HMRC uncertainty matters, but market reports, NGO critique, and academic estimates cannot substitute for linked taxpayer and asset data.

tax_residency_enforcement.note: Residence-based repair only converts into public value if HMRC can track residence, offshore income/gains, trusts, and transfer-of-assets effects across CRS/AEOI rails.

exit_tax_and_deemed_disposal_rails.note: The cube still lacks full deemed-disposal, remittance-basis transition, and trust/IHT restructuring data needed to separate real exit from tax planning.

gate_13_jurisdictional_mobility.why: Gate 13 remains watch: domicile-status privilege was narrowed, but FIG relief, trusts/IHT, behavioural exits, and ordinary-resident parity remain live proof burdens.

gate_10_measurement_uncertainty.why: HMRC/OBR administrative data and CRS rails are needed before reform impact can be certified rather than narrated.

evidence_debt_register.question: actual non-dom/nonresident migration after reform
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Use HMRC taxpayer residence/status data and OBR forecast updates to distinguish actual exits from advisory-market narratives.

evidence_debt_register.question: FIG claims by wealth/income cohort
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Publish or estimate FIG claims by income, wealth, arrival year, nationality/residence history, and tax paid so newcomer relief is not invisible.

evidence_debt_register.question: trust, IHT, and transfer-of-assets restructuring
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Track trust distributions, protected/trust status, transfer-of-assets claims, IHT changes, and offshore-asset relocation after the reform.

evidence_debt_register.question: revenue by cohort versus forecast
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Compare actual receipts with OBR uncertainty ranges and cohort-level behaviour, not aggregate receipts alone.

evidence_debt_register.question: property-market and asset-location response
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Measure high-value property transactions, overseas asset disclosure, and remittance behaviour around the reform window.

evidence_debt_register.question: ordinary long-term resident comparison
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Compare FIG/newcomer relief with the tax position of ordinary long-term residents to test whether status privilege has truly been removed.

policy_pathway: Keep the UK non-dom transition as a reform-watch case until HMRC/OBR data prove FIG take-up, trust/IHT response, asset movement, revenue, and ordinary-resident parity.
Treat exit-threat evidence as a counterweighted data problem, not a veto against residence-tax alignment.
